name: Mists of Mistvale
description: The Mists manifest without warning. The air cools rapidly, and visibility drops as a creeping frost covers the ground. The onset is often heralded by a sudden drop in temperature and the distant echo of forlorn whispers. Detection: Players can detect the incoming Mists with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check. This check can be made with advantage if the party can detect weather changes or is familiar with the region’s lore. Noticing it allows escape by running away from the expanding frost. Effects: Cold Exposure. Upon entering the Mists, creatures must make a DC 12 Constitution saving throw at the end of each hour or take 2d6 cold damage and suffer one level of exhaustion from the creeping frost. Reduced Visibility. The dense fog reduces visibility to 15 feet. Creatures within the Mists have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight. Undead Hordes. Every hour a creature spends in the Mists, there is a 20% chance to find a group of undead. The GM rolls a d10, and on a roll of 1 or 2, the creature will encounter a group of undeads emerging from the fog to attack. Navigation Challenge. The disorienting nature of the Mists imposes disadvantage on any Wisdom (Survival) checks made to navigate. Long-Term Exposure. Creatures that perish in the Mists rise as frozen undead after 24 hours. These undead are bound to the Mists and cannot leave its radius. Countermeasures: Casting protection from energy(cold)or similar magic can prevent the exhaustion from cold exposure. Carrying a beacon of warmth, such as a flame tongue weapon or everburning torch, can reduce the cold’s effect, granting advantage on the Constitution saving throw against cold exposure
